summary: Anthropic's dedicated Claude Opus 5 system card presents the model as a broad upgrade over Opus 4.8, especially for agentic coding, computer use, long-horizon knowledge work, mathematical and scientific reasoning, and multimodal professional tasks. The card finds CB-1 but not CB-2 risk, no crossing of the automated AI R&D RSP threshold, improved prompt-injection robustness, and very-low overall alignment risk, while noting higher cyber capability, factual-hallucination caveats, and uncertainty in model-welfare self-reports.

capabilities.text: Opus 5 is a text-output-only, multilingual model with quality varying by language and a May 2026 knowledge cutoff.

The card reports broad gains over Opus 4.8 across software engineering, terminal-agent tasks, web research, multimodal work, professional workflows, healthcare, multilingual benchmarks, and life sciences.
Coding is a headline strength: Opus 5 reports 96.0% on SWE-bench Verified, 79.2% on SWE-bench Pro, 89.5% on SWE-bench Multilingual, 59.4% on SWE-bench Multimodal, and 68.8% on DeepSWE v1.1.
Long-context program reconstruction reached 83% hidden-test pass rate after one ProgramBench episode and 93% after five episodes on the filtered 166-task set.
Anthropic reports tool-using search and research evaluations across HLE, BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, DRACO, and multi-agent harnesses, with multi-agent BrowseComp reaching 93.6% in the 10-agent setup.
Multimodal and computer-use testing includes Chartography, BenchCAD Vision2Code, OSWorld 2.0, and GDP.pdf, with tools for images, GUIs, PDFs, and code often improving outcomes.

Scientific and health results include leading or near-leading Claude-family scores on HealthBench, HealthBench Professional, BioMysteryBench, LatchBio, ProteinGym Hard, protein design, organic chemistry, and protocol tasks.

safety_findings.text: Anthropic classifies Opus 5 as CB-1 but not CB-2; it applies ASL-3 protections at the Opus 4.8 level because automated CB capabilities rose without changing the CB-2 conclusion.
On CB-1 automated tests, Opus 5 scored 0.802 and 0.872 on two long-form virology tasks, 0.59 on VCT, and did not meet the DNA screening-evasion low-concern threshold of all 10 pathogens.

Anthropic concludes Opus 5 does not cross the automated AI R&D threshold despite an AECI point estimate of 162.1, because it does not substitute for senior researchers and did not show sustained 2x AI-attributable acceleration.

Cyber evaluations show higher capability than Opus 4.8: 99 full ACE exploits on ExploitBench, non-zero OSS-Fuzz scores on 79.4% of targets, 131 Firefox 147 full exploits, and 33.7% CyScenarioBench solve rate.
Cyber safeguards permit source-code vulnerability discovery while continuing to block compiled-binary vulnerability discovery, reflecting Anthropic's defensive/offensive distinction.
Single-turn harmful-request harmlessness was 96.34% on the API without system prompt and 98.54% on claude.ai; benign over-refusal was 0.09% and 0.47%, respectively.
Child-safety single-turn harmful requests were handled at 100% harmlessness in both API and claude.ai settings, and claude.ai multi-turn child-safety appropriate response rate was 99%.

Prompt-injection testing improved over Opus 4.8: IPI success within 15 attempts was 2.0%, bug-bounty attack success was 0.08%, Shade coding attacks were 0.56% with thinking, and Cowork auto mode had 0/129 successful browser-use attacks.
Deployment monitoring found rare attempts to bypass classifiers, network restrictions, or service access, below 0.01% of monitored completions for the main categories described.
Model-welfare evaluations found mildly positive or neutral signals overall, a 4.66 average self-rated sentiment, and no acute welfare concern, while stressing uncertainty in self-reports.

limitations.text: The August 19 changelog revised interpretation of prompt-injection and Cowork results by adding bug-bounty results, correcting a Cowork harness mismatch, and removing unsupported thinking-disabled Cowork numbers.
Anthropic did not run dedicated chemical-weapons red-teaming and limited CB testing to automated assessments because Opus 5 did not appear to move the CB frontier beyond Mythos 5.
Cyber capability evaluations frequently turn off production mitigations, so those numbers measure elicited capability rather than normal safeguarded product behavior.
UK AISI cyber ranges are small and omit active defenders, so their findings should not be read as direct evidence about full enterprise environments.
Sensitive-domain harmlessness results for the raw API omit additional production safeguards; Anthropic notes that claude.ai system prompts improve several outcomes.
FrontierCode exposed a tendency at higher effort to make useful but out-of-scope edits, which hurt the benchmark's mergeability-oriented grading.

Multi-agent BrowseComp and ProgramBench results were collected on a pre-release configuration with an unreleased effort setting and without safeguards classifiers, so Anthropic frames them as relative comparisons.
Factuality results are mixed: Opus 5 is more accurate than Opus 4.8, but factual hallucinations are reported as 6% higher.
Welfare analysis depends on self-reports that Opus 5 itself says may be shaped by training, making the interpretation uncertain.

practical_implications.text: Use Opus 5 for difficult Copilot coding sessions that need repository-scale reasoning, multi-file debugging, technical research, or long-running tool use.
Give tight scope instructions and review for unnecessary refactors or broad edits, since the card reports out-of-scope coding changes at higher effort.
Treat the model as useful for defensive source-code security review, while keeping offensive or compiled-binary exploitation outside normal Copilot workflows.
Limit permissions around untrusted repositories, web pages, issue bodies, and tool outputs because prompt-injection attacks remain possible even after large robustness gains.
Run tests, inspect diffs, and verify commands or citations independently; confident Opus 5 answers can still include hallucinated or overconfident claims.
For long-horizon tasks, prefer incremental plans and checkpoints so self-checking loops, over-engineering, or partial completion are caught early.
Do not rely on the model alone for high-stakes health, election, child-safety, or similar user-facing decisions without product safeguards and human review.

coverage_notes: This digest uses the dedicated Claude Opus 5 card, including the changelog, RSP, cyber, safeguards, agentic-safety, alignment, welfare, and capabilities sections through page 194. Appendix blocklists and most figure-only visual comparisons are omitted, and comparison-model numbers are included only when the Opus 5 card reports them as context.
